title: Core affine reduced fibre embedding
statement: Let Z, S and S-prime be affine schemes [def-pc-fibre-product], with S-prime integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let g: Z to S and q: S-prime to S, and let eta-prime be a generic point with q(eta-prime)=eta. Let L, k-prime, E be fields with algebra structures kappa(eta) to L and k-prime, and L and k-prime to E, whose composites agree. Suppose k-prime/kappa(eta) is finite purely inseparable; j: Spec L to the eta fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is scheme-theoretically dominant with its base composite the algebra map; and e: kappa(eta-prime) to k-prime is a ring equivalence identifying the q residue map with the specified algebra map. Then there exists a kappa(eta-prime)-algebra structure on E and a scheme-theoretically dominant map from Spec E to the eta-prime fibre of the reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] of Z times_S S-prime. Its base composite is the spectrum of that algebra map, and the algebra map sends every x to the image of e(x) in E. No separable-generation assumption or conclusion occurs.

proof.text: Construct the residue-field algebra on E as the composition of e with k-prime to E. Write C for the original affine fibre ring and k for kappa(eta). Affine scheme-theoretic dominance of j identifies C with a k-subalgebra of L.

Flatness of k-prime over k gives an injection C tensor_k k-prime into L tensor_k k-prime. The latter is a finite-dimensional L-algebra whose prime spectrum is a singleton by pure inseparability. The compatible maps give a unital homomorphism to E, with prime kernel equal to the nilradical. Thus its reduction injects into E; the injection from C tensor_k k-prime also stays injective on reductions by detection of nilpotence.

Writing B-prime for the integral coordinate ring of S-prime, its generic residue field is its fraction field. Localization at its nonzero elements commutes with reduction. The compatibility he identifies the reduced pullback generic fibre ring with the reduction of C tensor_k k-prime. Compose the injections and take Spec. Injectivity gives scheme-theoretic dominance, and the tensor scalar maps give the base identity and compatibility with e.

theorem exists_reduced_generic_fibre_field_embedding_core
    {Z S S' : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine Z] [IsAffine S] [IsAffine S'] [IsIntegral S']
    (g : Z ⟶ S) (q : S' ⟶ S) (η : S) (η' : S') (hq : q η' = η)
    (hη' : IsGenericPoint η' Set.univ)
    (L k' E : Type u) [Field L] [Field k'] [Field E]
    [Algebra (S.residueField η) L] [Algebra (S.residueField η) k']
    [Algebra L E] [Algebra k' E]
    [Module.Finite (S.residueField η) k'] [IsPurelyInseparable (S.residueField η) k']
    (j : Spec (.of L) ⟶ g.fiber η) (hj : IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant j)
    (hjbase : j ≫ g.fiberToSpecResidueField η =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField η) L)))
    (e : S'.residueField η' ≃+* k')
    (he : e.toRingHom.comp
      (((S.residueFieldCongr hq).inv ≫ q.residueFieldMap η').hom) =
        algebraMap (S.residueField η) k')
    (hsquare : (algebraMap k' E).comp (algebraMap (S.residueField η) k') =
      (algebraMap L E).comp (algebraMap (S.residueField η) L)) :
    ∃ aE : Algebra (S'.residueField η') E,
      letI := aE
      ∃ h : Spec (.of E) ⟶
          ((pullback g q).nilradical.subschemeι ≫ pullback.snd g q).fiber η',
        IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant h ∧
        h ≫ ((pullback g q).nilradical.subschemeι ≫
          pullback.snd g q).fiberToSpecResidueField η' =
            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S'.residueField η') E)) ∧
        ∀ x : S'.residueField η',
          algebraMap (S'.residueField η') E x = algebraMap k' E (e x)
